Create a 12-second portrait gameplay concept from the supplied polished reference. Preserve this game's existing visual language throughout: flat elements stay flat; shaded elements retain the same kind of shading, material, depth and lighting. Never convert the game to another illustration/rendering style. The reference is the exact opening layout and inventory. Keep every fixed HUD word, number, functional color, camera projection, board boundary and character identity, except the explicitly authorized state updates below.

The creative priority is a striking improvement in GAME FEEL through ANIMATION, VFX AND AUDIO. Direct a beautifully timed, readable demonstration of the supplied legal moves: a clear anticipation, decisive travel, a satisfying contact/snap, an expressive but controlled settle and a quiet final-state hold. Make each interaction feel authored and responsive. Character actions may include a short blink, wingbeat, ear flick or gentle squash within their existing footprint; rigid tiles/cards/rings/board pieces remain rigid. No new gameplay action, extra piece, refill, combo, victory or reward.

VFX must speak the same visual language as the original. For flat artwork use short graphic strokes, opaque colored ticks and clean shape bursts. For shaded artwork use compact material-appropriate contact effects and existing-style highlights/soft particles. Do not introduce dimensional shadows, bloom or photoreal lighting to flat art. Do not flatten a shaded game. Localize accents to the actual touch, landing, merge or release; keep symbols legible and clear effects quickly. Keep the full screen and HUD visible. Board/puzzle cameras remain locked; an impact-heavy 3D game may have one extremely small recoil with immediate exact return, never a zoom, orbit or crop.

Audio carries equal craft: a distinct input sound, short motion accent, crisp material-specific contact and brief rewarding resolution for each real event, with clear rhythmic spacing. Include the supplied concise mechanics narration, natural and intelligible, with original understated music ducked beneath it and no recognizable tune. Avoid a constant wall of sound or a victory fanfare for partial progress. Sync accents to visible contact frames. The result should feel substantially more responsive and satisfying while unmistakably remaining the same game.

Execute only the following verified input/state sequence. Show each moved object continuously from its source to the correct destination. Preserve all unrelated pieces, slot counts, order, links, shadows and HUD values. Hold the exact specified partial result at the end. This is a look-and-feel proposal, not evidence of a Unity implementation.
